tool_args.rationale: All five pilot horizons are at or below 0.48, far short of the target H = 22.8. The slow-horizon probe directly tests whether the initially positive response weakens or reverses and helps separate adaptation amplitude from its time constant before fitting.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon law now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: At the pilot horizons, a slow adaptation term depends mainly on the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. Similar pilot fits can therefore give different forecasts at H = 22.8.
Finer trajectory sampling does not directly test whether the slow adaptation term saturates or reverses the short-window gain near the forecast horizon.
The auxiliary measurement does not constrain the slow adaptation term.

considered_alternatives.option: Sink-free dual-horizon or periodic harmonic model
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Neither accounts for the reported sink-gradient signature, and the pilot provides no evidence of periodicity.
